Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-0-transcribe-medium-0089", "row_sha256": "8e080e32cbba2d399a715df0ad6aeb6affa02686d5909b38134d04596ce0688d", "mode": "/transcribe", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Remove true hesitation and accidental restarts. Apply explicit corrections to the final stated intent. Preserve meaningful filler-like words and unfinished thoughts. Apply clearly spoken punctuation and list cues. Keep the supplied language.", "input": "um yesterday i joined the screen reader audit for the new booking page and checked it with the team in the small conference room we started with the trip search because that is where people reported losing their place when the results loaded mara read the page aloud while i followed the focus outline and noted each control that was skipped uh-huh she said when i asked whether the date picker had been tested with the keyboard she confirmed it had but the month change still announced only the new number and not the month name we also checked the filter panel on a narrow window the headings were in the right order and the apply button stayed reachable after the list expanded i heard one label read as unlabeled button on the first pass but it was correct after the page finished loading so i wrote down the timing and the browser version rather than calling it a repeatable defect we ended by comparing notes against the audit checklist and agreed to run that same date picker test again with the next build before sharing the findings with the design team", "output": "Yesterday, I joined the screen reader audit for the new booking page and checked it with the team in the small conference room. We started with the trip search because that is where people reported losing their place when the results loaded. Mara read the page aloud while I followed the focus outline and noted each control that was skipped. “Uh-huh,” she said when I asked whether the date picker had been tested with the keyboard. She confirmed it had, but the month change still announced only the new number and not the month name. We also checked the filter panel on a narrow window. The headings were in the right order, and the apply button stayed reachable after the list expanded. I heard one label read as “unlabeled button” on the first pass, but it was correct after the page finished loading, so I wrote down the timing and the browser version rather than calling it a repeatable defect. We ended by comparing notes against the audit checklist and agreed to run that same date picker test again with the next build before sharing the findings with the design team."}]
